title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 4
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Weekly passengers and buses allocated on five routes:

Route 2: 18,400 passengers, 7 buses
Route 5: 26,100 passengers, 12 buses
Route 9: 9,800 passengers, 3 buses
Route 14: 31,500 passengers, 15 buses
Route 21: 12,600 passengers, 5 buses

Which route carries the most passengers per bus?
options: A. Route 2
B. Route 5
C. Route 9
D. Route 14
E. Route 21
questions.explanation: Passengers divided by buses: Route 2 2,629, Route 5 2,175, Route 9 3,267, Route 14 2,100, Route 21 2,520. Route 9 is highest. The busiest route in total has the largest allocation and is not the most stretched.

questions.prompt:
Quarterly operating profit, in thousands:

Q1: 412
Q2: 388
Q3: 297
Q4: 281

In which quarter was the percentage fall from the previous quarter the largest?
options: A. Q2
B. Q4
C. The fall was equal in each quarter
D. Profit did not fall in any quarter
E. Q3
questions.explanation: Quarter on quarter: Q2 -5.8%, Q3 -23.5%, Q4 -5.4%. Q3 is the largest fall at -23.5%. Q4 loses fewer thousands and starts from a smaller base, giving a smaller percentage.

questions.prompt:
Share of a grocer's sales by category:

Own brand: 38%
Branded: 29%
Fresh: 16%
Frozen: 9%
Household: 5%
Other: 3%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for more than 80% of sales?
options: A. Three
B. Four
C. Two
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Largest first: 38 + 29 = 67%, then + 16 = 83%, which is still not above 80. Adding Frozen reaches 92%. So 3 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Eight values, in order: 8, 11, 11, 12, 14, 15, 19, 96

Which statement about these values is accurate?
options: A. The mean is smaller than the median
B. The range is smaller than the mean
C. The mean and median are equal
D. The mean is more than twice the median
E. The mode is larger than the mean
questions.explanation: Mean is 186/8 = 23.25; median is the average of the fourth and fifth values, 13. 23.25 is more than twice 13. The range is 88, far larger than the mean, and the mode is 11.

questions.prompt:
Two providers convert currency:

Provider F: no fixed fee, 1.9% of the amount
Provider G: GBP 12.00 fixed fee plus 0.4% of the amount

Select the amount at which the two cost the same AND the cheaper provider for a transfer of GBP 2,000.00.
options: A. GBP 800.00; Provider F is cheaper at GBP 2,000.00
B. GBP 800.00; Provider G is cheaper at GBP 2,000.00
C. GBP 1,000.00; Provider F is cheaper at GBP 2,000.00
D. GBP 600.00; Provider G is cheaper at GBP 2,000.00
E. The two never cost the same
questions.explanation: Equal when 0.019a = 12 + 0.004a, so a = 12/0.015 = GBP 800.00. At GBP 2,000.00: F charges GBP 38.00, G charges GBP 20.00, so Provider G is cheaper above the crossover.

questions.prompt:
A van can be bought for GBP 9,800.00 and sold after 5 years for GBP 3,200.00, with servicing of GBP 480.00 a year, or leased for GBP 195.00 a month with servicing included.

Select the cheaper option per year over five years AND the annual difference.
options: A. Leasing; GBP 540.00
B. Buying; GBP 500.00
C. Leasing; GBP 1,000.00
D. Buying; GBP 540.00
E. The two cost the same each year
questions.explanation: Buying costs GBP 9,800.00 − GBP 3,200.00 = GBP 6,600.00 of depreciation over 5 years, which is GBP 1,320.00 a year, plus GBP 480.00 servicing: GBP 1,800.00. Leasing is 12 × GBP 195.00 = GBP 2,340.00. Buying is cheaper by GBP 540.00 a year. Comparing the purchase price with a year of lease payments is the error.

questions.prompt:
Two crops on the same farm:

Wheat: 8.2 tonnes a hectare at GBP 195.00 a tonne, input cost GBP 640.00 a hectare
Barley: 6.9 tonnes a hectare at GBP 172.00 a tonne, input cost GBP 430.00 a hectare

Select the crop with the higher revenue per hectare AND the crop with the higher revenue per pound of input.
options: A. Wheat on revenue; Barley on revenue per pound of input
B. Wheat on both measures
C. Barley on revenue; Wheat on revenue per pound of input
D. Barley on both measures
E. The two crops are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Revenue a hectare: Wheat GBP 1,599.00, Barley GBP 1,186.80. Revenue per pound of input: Wheat 2.50, Barley 2.76. The crop earning more per hectare is not the one that turns inputs into revenue most efficiently.

questions.prompt:
Two loans of GBP 12,000.00, each with simple interest charged on the original sum:

Loan A: 6.1% a year over 5 years
Loan B: 4.9% a year over 7 years

Select the loan with the lower total interest AND the loan with the lower monthly repayment.
options: A. Loan A on both measures
B. Loan B on both measures
C. Loan B on total interest; Loan A on monthly repayment
D. Neither can be determined
E. Loan A on total interest; Loan B on monthly repayment
questions.explanation: Total interest: A GBP 3,660.00, B GBP 4,116.00. Monthly repayment spreads principal plus interest over the term: A GBP 261.00, B GBP 191.86. The cheaper loan overall costs more each month, because the shorter term concentrates the repayment.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): patients seen last year — Clinic A 4,200, Clinic B 2,700, Clinic C 5,600

SOURCE 2 (table): clinicians in post — Clinic A 6, Clinic B 3, Clinic C 9

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Additional staff should go where each clinician carries the heaviest caseload."

Which clinic should receive additional staff on that criterion?
options: A. Clinic A
B. Clinic B
C. Clinic C
D. All three carry equal caseloads
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Patients per clinician: Clinic A 700, Clinic B 900, Clinic C 622. Clinic B is heaviest. Clinic C sees the most patients in total, which Source 1 alone would suggest, but it also has the most clinicians.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our customer satisfaction score is 4.6 out of 5, so customers are happy with the service."

SOURCE 2 (method note): "The survey is sent to customers who have held an account for at least twelve months."

SOURCE 3 (table): 41% of new accounts are closed within the first six months.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Satisfaction has risen since last year
B. The score is inaccurate and should be discarded
C. The score describes customers who stayed, and excludes the large group who left early
D. Most customers are dissatisfied
E. The survey should be sent more frequently
questions.explanation: The sampling rule in Source 2 removes anyone who left inside a year, and Source 3 shows that group is large. The score may be correct about the customers surveyed while saying nothing about the ones the company lost — option B overstates, since the figure is not wrong, only narrow.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): units sold — April 1,180, May 1,240, June 1,420

SOURCE 2 (table): units sold in the same months last year — April 940, May 1,010, June 1,360

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Sales are growing month on month, so the new range is working."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Sales fell month on month this year
B. The new range has clearly caused the growth
C. Year-on-year growth accelerated over the three months
D. Last year's figures are irrelevant to the memo's claim
E. Sales rose month on month in both years, so the pattern may be seasonal rather than caused by the range
questions.explanation: This year rises 1,180 to 1,240 to 1,420; last year rose 940 to 1,010 to 1,360 across the same months, before the range existed. Year-on-year growth is April 26%, May 23%, June 4%, which narrows rather than accelerates.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): deliveries made, in thousands — Depot X 96, Depot Y 152, Depot Z 74

SOURCE 2 (table): rate of damaged deliveries — Depot X 1.4%, Depot Y 0.6%, Depot Z 2.9%

SOURCE 3 (email): "Compensation costs the same per damaged delivery wherever it happens."

Which depot generates the highest compensation cost?
options: A. Depot Z
B. Depot X
C. Depot Y
D. The three are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Damaged deliveries are volume multiplied by rate: Depot X 1,344, Depot Y 912, Depot Z 2,146. Depot Z has the worst rate and Depot Y the largest volume, but neither tops the count on its own.

questions.prompt:
A box holds only 20p and 50p coins, 40 coins in total. What is their total value?

(1) There are 26 coins of 20p.
(2) There are more 20p coins than 50p coins.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), 26 at 20p and 14 at 50p gives GBP 12.20 — sufficient. (2) only says the 20p coins are the majority, which allows 21 through 39 of them and many different totals.

questions.prompt:
A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?

(1) Its length is twice its width.
(2) Its width is 6 cm.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Perimeter 36 gives length + width = 18. From (1), 2w + w = 18, so w = 6 and l = 12, area 72 — sufficient. From (2), w = 6 gives l = 12 and the same area — also sufficient.

questions.prompt:
How many hours did a machine run last week?

(1) It produced 5,400 units.
(2) It produces 450 units an hour whenever it is running.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives output with no rate; (2) gives a rate with no output. Together, 5,400/450 = 12 hours — sufficient only in combination.

questions.prompt:
Is the mean age of a group of five people greater than 30?

(1) The youngest is 22.
(2) The oldest is 41.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The two extremes leave the middle three unconstrained: ages 22, 23, 23, 24, 41 average 26.6, while 22, 38, 39, 40, 41 average 36. Both are consistent with the statements, so the question is unanswered.

questions.prompt:
Which school receives the most funding per pupil?

School | Pupils | Annual funding | Teachers | Pass rate
Aldingham | 412 | GBP 1,284,000.00 | 63 | 41%
Barrowby | 268 | GBP 902,000.00 | 44 | 55%
Cranfold | 596 | GBP 1,690,000.00 | 82 | 38%
Deepdale | 184 | GBP 655,000.00 | 31 | 51%
Eversleigh | 350 | GBP 1,106,000.00 | 52 | 47%
Fenbrook | 478 | GBP 1,402,000.00 | 70 | 44%
options: A. Aldingham
B. Barrowby
C. Cranfold
D. Deepdale
E. Eversleigh
questions.explanation: Funding divided by pupils: Aldingham GBP 3,116.50, Barrowby GBP 3,365.67, Cranfold GBP 2,835.57, Deepdale GBP 3,559.78, Eversleigh GBP 3,160.00, Fenbrook GBP 2,933.05. Deepdale is highest. The school with the largest budget also has the most pupils and receives less for each of them.

questions.prompt:
How many schools have a pupil-to-teacher ratio above the mean ratio for the six?

School | Pupils | Annual funding | Teachers | Pass rate
Aldingham | 412 | GBP 1,284,000.00 | 63 | 41%
Barrowby | 268 | GBP 902,000.00 | 44 | 55%
Cranfold | 596 | GBP 1,690,000.00 | 82 | 38%
Deepdale | 184 | GBP 655,000.00 | 31 | 51%
Eversleigh | 350 | GBP 1,106,000.00 | 52 | 47%
Fenbrook | 478 | GBP 1,402,000.00 | 70 | 44%
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Two
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Ratios: Aldingham 6.5, Barrowby 6.1, Cranfold 7.3, Deepdale 5.9, Eversleigh 6.7, Fenbrook 6.8, with a mean of 6.57. Above it: Cranfold, Eversleigh, Fenbrook — 3 schools.

questions.prompt:
Which school has the greatest number of pupils passing?

School | Pupils | Annual funding | Teachers | Pass rate
Aldingham | 412 | GBP 1,284,000.00 | 63 | 41%
Barrowby | 268 | GBP 902,000.00 | 44 | 55%
Cranfold | 596 | GBP 1,690,000.00 | 82 | 38%
Deepdale | 184 | GBP 655,000.00 | 31 | 51%
Eversleigh | 350 | GBP 1,106,000.00 | 52 | 47%
Fenbrook | 478 | GBP 1,402,000.00 | 70 | 44%
options: A. Aldingham
B. Barrowby
C. Cranfold
D. Deepdale
E. Eversleigh
questions.explanation: Passing pupils are roll multiplied by pass rate: Aldingham 169, Barrowby 147, Cranfold 226, Deepdale 94, Eversleigh 165, Fenbrook 210. Cranfold is highest despite not having the best pass rate; the school with the best rate is Barrowby, whose roll is far smaller.

questions.prompt:
Rank the schools by funding (highest first) and separately by pass rate (highest first). Which school's two ranks differ most?

School | Pupils | Annual funding | Teachers | Pass rate
Aldingham | 412 | GBP 1,284,000.00 | 63 | 41%
Barrowby | 268 | GBP 902,000.00 | 44 | 55%
Cranfold | 596 | GBP 1,690,000.00 | 82 | 38%
Deepdale | 184 | GBP 655,000.00 | 31 | 51%
Eversleigh | 350 | GBP 1,106,000.00 | 52 | 47%
Fenbrook | 478 | GBP 1,402,000.00 | 70 | 44%
options: A. Aldingham
B. Barrowby
C. Eversleigh
D. Deepdale
E. Cranfold
questions.explanation: By funding: Cranfold, Fenbrook, Aldingham, Eversleigh, Barrowby, Deepdale. By pass rate: Barrowby, Deepdale, Eversleigh, Fenbrook, Aldingham, Cranfold. Rank gaps: Aldingham 2, Barrowby 4, Cranfold 5, Deepdale 4, Eversleigh 1, Fenbrook 2. Cranfold differs by 5.
